analysis: The units are base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md at base lines 838-1644. The file_changes range map is marked complete. It shows changes only at head lines 3541-3575: a new doc section, 'Cluster service listeners follow the cable and the pairing'. That section describes ClusterService.listenerChange restarting setup and control listeners when the cable port or address changes or a new pairing appears, and stopping them when no pairing exists. It also says pairing identity compares pins, label, link epoch and edge, never the edge secret, and that an unreadable pairing store changes nothing. None of the supplied base lines are changed. I reviewed them for context: the Nemotron Super durable checkpoint identity, cache-scope partitioning (T-041), GLM identity chain and VerifiedWeightHashStore (T-012/T-027), media refusals, calibration, and ChunkBatcher session-sink behavior (pre-existing, base 1547-1559). The new section is documentation only and is not visible in these units, so no line-cited regression can be raised. Questions for integration: verify the actual ClusterService.swift and ClusterSetupLinkExchange source changes. In particular, confirm that a listener keyed with a stale pairing reliably refuses handshakes, so revocation or re-pairing takes effect within 5 s. Also confirm that an unreadable pairing store failing to stop a listener (fail-static) does not keep a revoked peer authorized. The canonical threat model has no distributed-cluster trust boundary; a TB/threat entry for the inter-Mac cluster link may be needed if this surface is new. I have no evidence of whether this is new attack surface, so I recommend deeper review of the source files.
